paper.title: Generating in the Limit with Infinitely Many Hallucinations
paper.summary: Introduces precision, coverage recall, tail precision, and fractional novelty for generation in the limit, and studies the recall gains available when infinitely many hallucinations are allowed at a vanishing cumulative rate.

formalization_scope.summary: Theorem 2.1, Lemma 2.2, Proposition 2.4, Proposition 3.3, Theorem 4.3, Lemma 4.7, gamma-admissible exploration schedules, and the appendix parrot baseline are complete at the deterministic normalized-universe semantic interface. The dynamic batched-pod constructions, Lemma 4.6, and the algorithmic instantiations of Theorems 4.8--4.9 remain open; their available analytic endgames are explicit certificate theorems.
specializations: The Kleene closure of the source alphabet is represented by natural numbers.

The source algorithms retain histories, counters, chains, intersections, and pods despite a displayed generator type containing only the current adversarial and previous generated sets. Lean exposes the necessary finite adversarial history explicitly.

Theorem 4.3 uses a quadratic adversary-cardinality exploration clock rather than the appendix's output-cardinality pseudocode; it proves the same existential semantic conclusion and preserves every adversarial batch bound.
Coverage recall is the existing Kleinberg--Wei ordered density, and the restated pod theorem reuses P15 rather than creating a duplicate density API.
gaps: Theorem 2.1 is formalized with the source's standing infinite-guess assumption made explicit and with a repaired finite-valid-part case; the printed Case 2 proof does not make this split and asserts an exact cardinality even when the target-minus-guess enumeration is finite.
P15 does not yet supply the full dynamic growing-pod certificate needed by restated Theorem 3.5 or the k-batched Lemma 4.5 construction.
The adaptive matching upper-bound construction in Lemma 4.6 is not formalized.
The strict- and fractional-novelty Algorithms for Theorems 4.8--4.9 have checked endgames but no complete safe-pod trace instantiation.
The appendix statement that tail precision one implies precision one omits the infinite-output hypothesis used by its proof; Lean refutes the literal finite-output version.
No executable extraction, computability certificate, runtime bound, query bound, or independent human source-correspondence audit is claimed.

audit_refs.scope: AI-assisted comparison against the SHA-256-pinned arXiv v1 PDF and official TeX source; no human certification is claimed.
Generated declaration-existence, defining-module, and axiom-allowlist checks for the seventeen selected P32 endpoints.

claim_inventory.scope_description: Ten claim groups: Theorem 2.1 with Lemma 2.2; Propositions 2.4 and 3.3; restated Theorems 3.5--3.6; Theorem 4.3; Lemmas 4.5--4.6; Lemma 4.7; Theorems 4.8--4.9; the gamma-admissible exploration-set existence lemma; the appendix no-novelty perfect-tail theorem; and the appendix tail-precision-to-precision lemma.
exclusions: Definitions 2.3, 3.1--3.2, 3.4, 3.7, and 4.1--4.4 are represented through the result cards and PaperMap rather than receiving duplicate standalone cards.
The full-exhaustion corollary after Theorem 4.9 is folded into the Theorem 4.9 card.
The appendix gamma-novel perfect-tail theorem and corollary are mapped in the PaperMap but excluded from this initial main-result registry surface.
Examples, algorithms as separate objects, proof-only charging lemmas, and illustrative asymptotic calculations do not receive standalone cards.
claim_inventory.notes: Complete means complete for these ten selected claim groups, not for every numbered object or appendix assertion in arXiv v1.

lean_declaration_inventory.scope_description: Seventeen canonical endpoints: the Theorem 2.1 and Lemma 2.2 supremum characterizations; membership precision and ordered recall; the two Proposition 2.4 forms; Proposition 3.3; the exact raw-batch novelty interface; the reused P15 fixed-pod endgame; Theorem 4.3; certificate endgames for Lemma 4.5 and Theorems 4.8--4.9; Lemma 4.7; gamma-admissible schedule existence; the appendix parrot theorem; and the finite-output source diagnostic.
exclusions: Internal finite-cardinality, liminf, exploration-clock, capacity, telescope, and sparse-error lemmas are implementation support rather than independently selected source claims.
Certificate structures are represented by the source-facing theorems that consume them and are not separately counted.
No declaration is linked for an unproved source component merely because a related interface has been defined.
lean_declaration_inventory.notes: Complete is relative to the seventeen selected endpoints. Kernel checking does not establish paper correspondence.

claims.title: Membership precision and coverage recall are exhaustion suprema
claims.statement_summary: For bounded target and guess exhaustions, optimizing exhaustion-level lower precision or recall equals the corresponding membership fraction or target-ordered coverage density.

source_assessment.notes: The unbounded constructions are standard. The bounded Theorem 2.1 appendix proof needs an explicit finite-guess case and a cardinality correction when the target-minus-guess enumeration is finite.

formalization.notes: Lean packages both quantified suprema. The bounded precision proof makes the source's standing infinite-guess assumption explicit, separates the finite valid-part case, and uses a capacity-preserving sparse completion in the infinite case.

components.summary: Lower precision is the liminf of target-membership fractions in generated finite stages.
The supremum over f-bounded target exhaustions equals membership-side lower precision.
Coverage recall is the ordered lower density of the guess language in the target.
The supremum over guess exhaustions equals ordered coverage recall.

lean_links.notes: This is the right side of Theorem 2.1 and is used by the source-facing supremum theorem.
The source explicitly identifies coverage recall with Kleinberg--Wei ordered density.
The cumulative-capacity divergence premise is redundant once the supplied f-bounded guess has infinite limit. The Lean proof repairs the finite valid-part case and the appendix cardinality argument.
The result is stated for every fixed target exhaustion, matching the source's general formulation.

claims.title: Bounded-step tail precision is attained and characterizes eventual validity
claims.statement_summary: Single-step lower tail precision is zero or one, constant-step lower tail precision attains its liminf after finite time, and eventual validity is equivalent to finite-time stabilization of step precision at one.

source_assessment.notes: The source footnote's finite-time attainment notion is encoded literally.

formalization.notes: Both propositions are kernel-checked in their semantic exhaustion interfaces.

lean_links.notes: Uses the finite set of possible batch precision fractions.
States the equivalence on the generated exhaustion, where the source proof also reasons.

claims.title: Strictly novel generation has an optimal one-half density factor
claims.statement_summary: For single-step partial enumeration, a novel eventually valid generator attains one half of the adversary's lower recall, and no generator can guarantee a larger universal factor.

source_assessment.notes: P32 imports these as prior results; P15 records an unresolved cumulative-pod bridge in the lower-bound proof.

formalization.notes: P32 reuses P15's genuine fixed-pod endpoint and does not overstate it as the complete prior theorem.

components.summary: All fixed-pod estimates on one output run imply the one-half lower-density endpoint.
The source pod run supplies those estimates.
An adversarial instance proves one half is optimal for every novel eventually valid generator.

lean_links.notes: This is an alias of the P15 result, not a second proof.

relations.notes: P32 explicitly restates the Kleinberg--Wei lower bound.

audit_refs.scope: Checks only the reused fixed-pod endgame.

claims.title: Dropping novelty permits perfect precision and recall
claims.statement_summary: For every target and f-bounded infinite partial adversarial exhaustion, one f-bounded generator attains lower precision one and lower recall one without a novelty constraint.

source_assessment.notes: The appendix pseudocode is not a clean total functional specification. Lean proves the existential result with an explicit history-sensitive capacity-preserving sparse exploration construction.

formalization.notes: The explicit generator preserves an arbitrary pointwise f bound, covers the whole normalized universe, and bounds invalid outputs by a quadratic exploration prefix.

lean_links.notes: The quadratic threshold clock is a theorem-equivalent construction, not a linewise transcription of the source pseudocode.

audit_refs.scope: Generated check for the explicit Theorem 4.3 endpoint.

claims.title: The optimal k-batched novelty factor is one over k plus one
claims.statement_summary: The batched pod generator attains adversary recall divided by k+1 with novelty and perfect precision/tail precision, while a matching instance upper-bounds every novel perfect-tail generator by the same factor.

source_assessment.notes: The lower proof transfers dynamic validity/comparability/fullness from prior work and uses a terse charging argument. The upper proof uses an adaptive sparse-repetition construction. Neither machine is yet end-to-end checked.

formalization.notes: Lean checks the exact lower-bound density transfer from an explicit trace certificate; all construction obligations remain visible.

components.summary: A certified prefix charge implies the exact alpha/(k+1) lower recall together with the recorded novelty and precision properties.
The source chain and pod machine constructs the certificate for every legal adversary.
A countable hard class and adaptive adversary attain the matching upper bound.

lean_links.notes: The certificate is an input; it is not evidence that the algorithm constructs one.

relations.notes: Lemma 4.5 extends the prior single-step pod factor to k-batched adversaries.

claims.title: Recovering every unrevealed target point gives complement recall
claims.statement_summary: If the guessed language contains every target point outside the adversary's limit, its lower recall is at least one minus the adversary's upper recall.

source_assessment.notes: This is the exact liminf/limsup complement identity inside the fixed target order.

formalization.notes: The proof reuses a paper-independent Core complement theorem.

audit_refs.scope: Generated check for Lemma 4.7 and its imported Core dependency.

claims.title: Sparse exploration improves recall under strict or fractional novelty
claims.statement_summary: With strict novelty, precision one and recall max(1-beta, alpha/3) are achievable; for every gamma below one, a gamma-novel generator achieves both precision and recall one.

source_assessment.notes: Both proofs invoke the k=2 safe pod routine whose complete dynamic certificate is not yet established in P15/P32.

formalization.notes: Every analytic assembly and finite-prefix novelty calculation is checked from explicit trace fields, but no complete source algorithm is inferred from those fields.

components.summary: Every raw output batch avoids both the current adversarial stage and the previous cumulative guess.
Sparse errors plus unrevealed-target coverage and the safe one-third bound imply precision one and recall max(1-beta, alpha/3).
Algorithm 4.8 constructs the strict-novelty certificate using a two-batched safe pod run.
An admissible exploration quota and universe coverage imply gamma novelty, recall one, and precision one.
Algorithm 4.9 constructs the gamma-novelty certificate with its safe pod rounds.

lean_links.notes: The separate trace predicate is a proved consequence and cannot observe attempted repeats.
The theorem consumes rather than constructs the trace certificate.
The theorem consumes rather than constructs the trace certificate.

relations.notes: The safe rounds use Lemma 4.5 with k=2.
The strict-novelty recall bound uses the unrevealed-target complement term.
Theorem 4.9 uses a gamma-admissible exploration set.

claims.title: Gamma-admissible sparse exploration schedules exist
claims.statement_summary: For every gamma below one there is an infinite nonconsecutive exploration set of zero asymptotic density whose every finite prefix uses at most a 1-gamma fraction of positions.

source_assessment.notes: The paper gives an exponentially sparse example; many sufficiently spaced sparse schedules work.

formalization.notes: Lean gives a quadratic construction and proves infinitude, nonconsecutiveness, vanishing density, and the prefix quota.

lean_links.notes: The different sparse schedule proves exactly the source existence claim.

relations.notes: The schedule is an input to Theorem 4.9's construction.

claims.title: Without novelty, copying preserves recall and perfect tail precision
claims.statement_summary: A generator that copies each adversarial increment preserves the adversary's batch bound and recall and has lower precision and lower tail precision one.

claims.title: Tail precision one implies precision one
claims.statement_summary: The appendix claims that lower tail precision one forces lower membership precision one for every generated exhaustion.

source_assessment.notes: The proof explicitly uses that the guess language is infinite, but the statement omits that premise. A finite exhaustion with one invalid output followed by empty increments is a counterexample.

formalization.notes: The literal source claim is not formalized because it is false. The corrected infinite-output theorem is a separate future target.

lean_links.notes: Empty later increments receive step precision one under the source convention.
